title: Consolidate scatter/gather staging and CPU->GPU handoff to reduce pipeline jitter
creator: Asha Rao
description: We observe tail latency spikes and elevated host CPU utilization caused by many small scatter/gather memcpy ops and uneven threadpool load during prefill->decode handoff. This ticket implements a "staging consolidation" layer and a handshake shaper that: (1) groups scatter/gather fragments into coalesced staging slabs, (2) applies NUMA-aware pinned allocations to reduce cross-node traffic, (3) exposes lightweight kernel-selection hints based on sequence-length histograms to the scheduler, and (4) throttles decode dispatches with token-aware backpressure to avoid saturating GPU submission threads. The goal is to lower host-side overhead while preserving decode latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end latency for short-prefill workloads reduces by >= 15% compared to baseline
Host CPU user+system utilization per GPU reduces by >= 25% under 400-token average workloads
Number of memcpy syscalls per request reduced by >= 60% for medium-length requests
No regression in model output correctness or KV cache semantics (sanity tests pass)
notes_updates: 2025-02-14 - Created: initial problem statement and proposed approach. Identified hot path: scatter/gather memcpy in host staging during prefill aggregation.

2025-02-18 - Spike results: microbenchmarked scatter->staging consolidator. Consolidation reduced syscall count by 3.7x and improved single-request prefill latency by 9% on rtx-a100 nodes. Details: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/ENG-783456+spike

2025-02-21 - Design decision: implement a unified slab allocator per NUMA domain + a 'flip' commit that atomically hands coalesced slabs to the GPU submission thread to avoid per-fragment ownership locks. Trade-off: increased transient host memory for short periods, but far fewer synchronization events.
2025-02-25 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 implements slab allocator, consolidation API, and unit tests. Marked WIP for perf harness integration.

2025-03-01 - Perf run #3: integrated with kernel-hint telemetry. Observed p95 improvement 12% after enabling kernel hints; combined with consolidation reached 18% in synthetic workloads. Noted small regression for very large sequences (>8k) due to extra copy; mitigated by bypass path for >4k lengths.
2025-03-03 - Current: integration tests green. Canary rollout planned to 5% of dedicated clusters next week. TODO: add rollout metric dashboards and update docs for runtime config knobs.
review_feedback: 2025-02-22 - Review from Jordan Kim (runtime): suggested adding a bypass for jumbo sequences to avoid double-copy. Accepted and implemented; added tests.
2025-02-26 - Review from Priya Patel (infra): requested NUMA binding be configurable per deployment class; added config flag and sane defaults.
2025-03-02 - Security review note from SRE: ensure staging slabs zero out before reuse to avoid leaking customer memory across requests. Implemented zeroing-on-free in allocator.
2025-03-03 - PM review (Liam O'Connor): verify rollout rollback conditions and alerting thresholds. Defined thresholds in monitoring section of PR.
